Account fixtures, recorded live on 2026-10-15

Each <server>.json is a replay recording: every statement myflames sent and
the exact `mysql --batch` text (or client error) it got back, captured by a
recording MySQLConnection while running privileges.read_privileges (one
session per account in "sessions") and accounts.list_accounts and
accounts.read_account as root ("reads"). Tests replay them by exact SQL.

Servers (throwaway Docker containers, removed after recording; client:
mysql 8.0.45 from Homebrew):
  mysql-8.0.json      mysql:8.0      8.0.46
  mysql-8.4.json      mysql:8.4      8.4.11
  mysql-9.7.json      mysql:9.7      9.7.2
  mariadb-10.11.json  mariadb:10.11  10.11.19-MariaDB
  mariadb-11.4.json   mariadb:11.4   11.4.13-MariaDB

Scenario (same on every server where the engine allows it):
  databases shop (table orders, procedure p, function f), db_x, dbAx;
  acct_admin  GRANT ALL ON *.* WITH GRANT OPTION (MySQL: every static and
              dynamic privilege, SYSTEM_USER included);
  acct_ops    CREATE USER, PROCESS, RELOAD, SELECT on mysql; MySQL also
              CONNECTION_ADMIN, ROLE_ADMIN; MariaDB also CONNECTION ADMIN;
  acct_app    roles r_read (default), r_write (MariaDB: WITH ADMIN OPTION),
              MySQL r_sys (holds SYSTEM_USER, not active), MySQL mandatory
              role r_mand (PROCESS; active on 9.7 where
              activate_mandatory_roles defaults ON, listed but inactive on
              8.0 and 8.4), MariaDB nested role r_nested under r_read;
              column grants SELECT (a, b), INSERT (a) and table UPDATE on
              shop.orders; EXECUTE on PROCEDURE shop.p; EXECUTE, ALTER
              ROUTINE on FUNCTION shop.f; SELECT on `db\_x` (literal),
              INSERT on `db_x` and DELETE on `shop%` (wildcards);
  acct_proxy  PROXY on acct_app@%; on MariaDB 11.4 also expired with
              MAX_USER_CONNECTIONS 3, MAX_STATEMENT_TIME 2.5 and PASSWORD
              EXPIRE INTERVAL 30 DAY (two SHOW CREATE USER rows);
  MySQL only: partial_revokes ON; acct_pr GRANT SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE ON *.*
              with REVOKE INSERT, UPDATE ON mysql.* and REVOKE SELECT ON db_x.*;
              acct_cu CREATE USER only;
  MariaDB only: PUBLIC with SLAVE MONITOR and SELECT on pubdb.*; acct_ed
              IDENTIFIED VIA ed25519 USING ... OR unix_socket; acct_super
              SUPER and CREATE USER (on 11.4 its password is expired, so its
              session records error 1820).

Passwords and hashes in these files belong to throwaway accounts on
containers that no longer exist. They are kept on purpose: the tests assert
that no hash, USING string or AS 0x... form ever leaves the parser.
